glossary_metadata.name: sec-edgar
glossary_metadata.description: SEC EDGAR filing types, entity identifiers, and regulatory concepts

terms.definition: Unique numeric identifier assigned by the SEC to every entity that files with the Commission. Used as the primary company identifier throughout the pipeline.
terms.cde_rationale: Core entity identifier critical for cross-system joins and audit trails.

terms.definition: Unique identifier for each filing submitted to SEC EDGAR. Format: XXXXXXXXXX-YY-ZZZZZZ. Used to trace any data point back to its source filing.
terms.cde_rationale: Primary filing identifier critical for source traceability and regulatory audit.

terms.definition: Official company name as registered with the SEC. May differ from commonly used brand names (e.g., 'MICROSOFT CORPORATION' vs 'Microsoft Corp.').
terms.cde_rationale: Core entity identifier critical for cross-system joins and audit trails.

terms.definition: A document submitted to and accepted by the SEC through the EDGAR system. Includes periodic reports (10-K, 10-Q), current reports (8-K), and amendments (10-K/A, 10-Q/A).
Date the filing was officially submitted to and accepted by the SEC. Critical for determining the timeline of financial disclosures and for amendment tracking.
terms.cde_rationale: Filing temporal metadata critical for amendment detection and regulatory timeline analysis.

terms.definition: A revised SEC filing (form type ending in '/A', e.g., 10-K/A, 10-Q/A) that corrects or updates a previously submitted filing. Amendments supersede the original filing's values for the same reporting period and concept.
Standard Industrial Classification code. A four-digit code assigned by the SEC that classifies a company's primary line of business. Used for industry-level analysis and peer comparison.
